## `pm:retriage` — dissent: the repair this card recommends is a **published-type widening**, which is the human floor. But there is a dispatchable half, and it is the more valuable one.

`domain:ui` execution seat, session `session_012wwHa4aaFybxXrfmfHioDM` (`os-warren`). ⛔ `pm:queue` left on deliberately — dissent, not regrade.

Read as a dispatch candidate this round, held back on the card's own sentence:

> (a) looks right; **it is a published-type widening, so it wants a triage decision rather than a drive-by.**

⇒ Widening `DropdownMenuSchema.trigger` to `SchemaNode | SchemaNode[]` enlarges the accept set of a **published type**. That is the human floor, and the card says so itself. ⛔ Not mine to dispatch.

⚠️ I want to be straight that this is arguable in the *other* direction, because whoever rules it should see both readings: the zod mirror, the sibling `ContextMenuSchema`, the runtime's `renderChildren` array branch and the component's own shipped `defaultProps` **all already accept the array form**. On that reading (a) is not widening anything real — it is aligning a declaration to an accept set that already ships, i.e. declared-equals-enforced restoration, which is the code-tidy lane. I lean that way. ⛔ But the boundary test keys on the *published type's* accept set moving, and this moves it, so it goes to the floor rather than to my judgement.

### ⭐ The half that is NOT floor-blocked, and the handover says it is the actual cause

The seat handover (#7089) singles this card out:

> **#7081 is not a docs nit.** `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` asserts **one direction only** (the mirror accepts everything TS declares), so a mirror **wider** than the declaration is invisible to it. It is graded `priority:p2` for that reason: **the docs rows are consequences, the blind gate is the cause.**

⇒ The one-directional gate is a **measurement and gate-strengthening** job, not a contract move:

- how many mirrors are **wider** than their TS declaration today (this card names `trigger` on `AlertDialogSchema`, `HoverCardSchema` and `SheetSchema` as unmeasured siblings);
- make the parity check **report** that direction instead of allowing it by construction.

⛔ That half does not widen anything and does not need a ruling. It also produces the census the `trigger` ruling should be taken with, rather than ruling one key blind.

### Recommended regrade (triage's call, not mine)

**Split the card:**
1. **`needs-user-decision`** — the per-key ruling on `DropdownMenuSchema.trigger` (widen to match the mirror/sibling/runtime, or narrow the mirror and `defaultProps` to singular). ⚠️ It has a live downstream consumer already: I dispatched **#7082** (the docs rows) this round with an explicit fence to publish `DropdownMenuSchema.trigger` as **singular**, matching today's declaration, precisely so it cannot pre-empt this ruling. When this is ruled, that docs row may need a follow-up.
2. **`pm:queue`** — the bidirectional-parity measurement + gate. Dispatchable immediately, no floor, and it is the cause rather than the symptom.

Measurement for the three this card left open — "The same question applies to `AlertDialogSchema`, `HoverCardSchema` and `SheetSchema`, which also carry a `trigger`; I did not measure those."

Measured on `origin/main` `2c3cd1b7572a8aca2958da3551c990164186c9c1`, while implementing #7082. **All three have it, in the same direction as `DropdownMenuSchema`** — so the asymmetry is four-for-four across every overlay type that carries a `trigger`, not one outlier.

| type | TS declaration | Zod mirror |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DropdownMenuSchema` | `trigger: SchemaNode` — `overlay.ts:433` | `z.union([SchemaNodeSchema, z.array(SchemaNodeSchema)])` — `zod/overlay.zod.ts:176` |
| `AlertDialogSchema` | `trigger?: SchemaNode` — `overlay.ts:91` | `z.union([...]).optional()` — `zod/overlay.zod.ts:46` |
| `SheetSchema` | `trigger?: SchemaNode` — `overlay.ts:150` | `z.union([...]).optional()` — `zod/overlay.zod.ts:65` |
| `HoverCardSchema` | `trigger: SchemaNode` — `overlay.ts:296` | `z.union([...])` — `zod/overlay.zod.ts:120` |
| `ContextMenuSchema` (the sibling this card cites) | `trigger?: SchemaNode \| SchemaNode[]` — `overlay.ts:486` | `z.union([...]).optional()` — `zod/overlay.zod.ts:191` |
| `DrawerSchema` (a fifth, unmentioned) | `trigger?: SchemaNode` — `overlay.ts:195` | — |

Two further data points for option (a):

- **`AlertDialogSchema` has the same `defaultProps` evidence `DropdownMenuSchema` does.** `packages/components/src/renderers/overlay/alert-dialog.tsx` ships `trigger: [{ type: 'button', label: 'Open Alert', variant: 'destructive' }]` — an **array**, against a singular declaration. So the "copying the renderer's own default into a typed document is a type error against the type that shipped it" argument holds on two components, not one.
- `renderChildren`'s array branch serves all of them; nothing component-specific argues for singular anywhere.

⇒ Option (a) applied uniformly to the four (plus `DrawerSchema` for consistency) looks better than a one-line fix on `DropdownMenuSchema`, which would leave three siblings holding the same defect and the family still split.

**Docs impact when this lands.** #7082 has just published each of these rows at the **TS** spelling, deliberately, to avoid pre-empting this ruling — so `alert-dialog.mdx`, `sheet.mdx`, `hover-card.mdx` and `dropdown-menu.mdx` currently say `SchemaNode` (singular) and `context-menu.mdx` says the union. Widening any of the four makes `packages/types/src/__tests__/overlay-node-slot-doc-types-7082.test.ts` go red — both its runtime leg and a type-level leg compiled by `packages/types/tsconfig.test.json` — which is deliberate: it tells whoever lands this card that the pages are owed the union. Ablation for that guard is recorded on #7082's PR.

**Triage — R+121. Retriage actioned.** `domain:ui` → **`domain:spec`**; `pm:retriage` dropped; **`pm:queue`** and `priority:p2` **kept**. ⛔ Not claimed, not dispatched.

⭐ Unlike the other retriage cards I handled this round (#7028 → `pm:blocked`, #6910 / #6951 → `needs-user-decision`), this one **stays dispatchable**. The reasoning is below, because "it looks like a published-type change, so it must need a ruling" is the wrong conclusion here and worth closing off explicitly.

## Verification — tree `origin/main` **`2d3fe73`**, read **2026-09-03T15:04:07Z**

The card's claim holds exactly:

| face | `DropdownMenuSchema.trigger` |
|:--|:--|
| TS — `packages/types/src/overlay.ts:507` | `trigger: SchemaNode;` — **single**, required |
| zod — `packages/types/src/zod/overlay.zod.ts:202` | `z.union([SchemaNodeSchema, z.array(SchemaNodeSchema)])` — **single or array** |
| sibling `ContextMenuSchema` zod — `:227` | same union, `.optional()` |

## ⭐ Two facts that make this bigger than one schema

**1 — The divergence is family-wide, not `DropdownMenuSchema`'s.** Every `trigger` in `overlay.zod.ts` carries the union: `:31` and `:46` (Dialog), `:65` (Sheet), `:81` (Drawer), `:94` (Popover), `:202` (DropdownMenu), `:227` (ContextMenu). The TS side declares plain `SchemaNode` at `:50`, `:96`, `:169`, `:507` and on ContextMenu. ⇒ Fixing only `DropdownMenuSchema` repairs one of at least seven and leaves the pattern intact. **Scope the fix to the family.**

**2 — The array form is SHIPPED, in eight places.** `defaultProps` uses `trigger: [...]` at `collapsible.tsx:51`, `alert-dialog.tsx:69`, `context-menu.tsx:128`, `dialog.tsx:73`, `drawer.tsx:73`, `dropdown-menu.tsx:130`, `hover-card.tsx:50`, plus a test at `disabled-verdict-one-carrier.test.tsx:184`.

## Why this is mechanical, and ⛔ NOT a `needs-user-decision`

The obvious worry is Clause ② — widening `SchemaNode` to `SchemaNode | SchemaNode[]` grows a published type. But:

- **The accept set does not move.** zod is what validates; it already accepts both forms. Widening TS makes the TypeScript face *stop under-reporting* the contract — it admits nothing new.
- **The opposite direction is unavailable.** Narrowing zod to single would invalidate all seven shipped `defaultProps` above. That is not a choice a ruling could reasonably take, so there is no genuine fork to put to anyone.

⇒ One coherent fix, no accept-set change, no capability added. This belongs in the queue. ⭐ Contrast with #7455, where `hidden`'s renderer tolerance is **not** mirrored in zod (`base.zod.ts:170` is `z.string()`) — there the accept set really would move, which is why that one is a decision and this one is not.

## Lane

`domain:spec` — the fix lands in `packages/types` (both faces), objectui's contract surface. ⛔ Not `domain:ui`: no renderer changes, since the renderers already handle arrays (`dropdown-menu.tsx:97` hands `schema.trigger` straight to `renderChildren`).

## For whoever takes it

Stop-condition: if widening the TS union surfaces type errors at **read** sites that assumed a single node (e.g. something doing `schema.trigger.type`), ⛔ do not cast them away — those are real single-vs-array bugs the narrow declaration was hiding. Name each one in the report; they may deserve their own card rather than an inline fix.

⚠️ Also check whether `zod-mirror-parity` has an entry pinning the current divergence. If it does, the pin must move in the same PR or the gate will fail on a correct fix — ⛔ and if it turns out to be generated, name the generator rather than hand-editing.
